etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English rop, rope, from Old English rāp (“rope, cord, cable”), from Proto-West Germanic *raip, from Proto-Germanic *raipaz, *raipą (“rope, cord, band, ringlet”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁roypnós (“strap, band, rope”), from *h₁reyp- (“to peel off, tear; border, edge, strip”).

definitions.definition: (uncountable) Thick strings, yarn, monofilaments, metal wires, or strands of other cordage that are twisted together to form a stronger line.
(countable) An individual length of such material.
(slang, vulgar) A shot of semen released during ejaculation.
A cohesive strand of something.

quote.text: Jimmy began to scream and ropes of spit shot from his mouth.

definitions.definition: (dated) A continuous stream.

quote.citation: 1852, John Bourne, A Treatise on the Screw Propeller: With Various Suggestions of Improvement, page 38:
quote.text: The principle of any such device should be to pull on the vessel by a rope of water passing in at the bow and out at the stern.

definitions.definition: (baseball) A hard line drive.
(ceramics) A long thin segment of soft clay, either extruded or formed by hand.
(computer science) A data structure resembling a string, using a concatenation tree in which each leaf represents a character.
(military, uncountable) A kind of chaff (material dropped to interfere with radar) consisting of foil strips with paper chutes attached.
(Jainism) A unit of distance equivalent to the distance covered in six months by a god flying at ten million miles per second.

quote.citation: 2001, “Review of Metaphysical Teaching”, in Nagendra Kr. Singh, editor, Encyclopaedia of Jainism‎[2], →ISBN, page 7522:
quote.text: The central strip of the loka, the Middle World, represents its smallest area, being only one rope wide and one hundred thousand leagues high,  […]

definitions.definition: (jewelry) A necklace of at least one meter in length.
(nautical) Cordage of at least one inch in diameter, or a length of such cordage.
(archaic) A unit of length equal to twenty feet.
(slang) Rohypnol.
(slang, usually in the plural) Semen being ejaculated.
(with "the") Death by hanging.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ropen, rope (“to form ropes”), from rop (“rope”); see above.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To tie (something) with rope.
(transitive) To throw a rope (or something similar, e.g. a lasso, cable, wire, etc.) around (something).
(intransitive) To climb by means of a rope or ropes.

quote.citation: 1984, G. F. Dutton, The Ridiculous Mountains, page 153:
quote.text: We roped down to the platform selected for the bivouac; set up our bags and brewed a reasonable meal.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To be formed into rope; to draw out or extend into a filament or thread.

quote.citation: 1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Life of Henry the Fift”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene v]:
quote.text: Let us not hang like roping icicles / Upon our houses' thatch.

definitions.definition: (Internet slang, intransitive) To commit suicide, particularly by hanging.

quote.citation: 2019, anonymous, quoted in Julia Rose DeCook, "Curating the Future: The Sustainability Practices of Online Hate Groups", dissertation submitted to Michigan State University, page 153:
quote.text: In figure 71, the poster Brahcel notes that he “almost roped” because he could not find the community  […]

quote.citation: 2020, Joshua A. Segalewitz, "'You Don't Understand... It's Not About Virginity': Sexual Markets, Identity Construction, and Violent Masculinity on an Incel Forum Board", thesis submitted to the University of Dayton, page 36:
quote.text: ToxicAlcoholSyndrome explains that his, “dreams are all really depressing and vivid, so… I’m constantly in a bad mood and know in the back of my brain, I need to rope.”

quote.citation: 2021, Laura Bates, From Incels to Pickup Artists: The Truth about Extreme Misogyny and How it Affects Us All, unnumbered page:
quote.text: Another man wrote that the only reason he hasn't “roped” (incel terminology for death by suicide) is he didn't want to ruin his family's Christmas.

etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English rop (“gut, intestine”), from Old English rop, ropp; compare Middle Dutch rop, roppe (“fish guts”).

The modern pronunciation results from phonological assimilation to Etymology 1.

definitions.definition: (in the plural) The small intestines.
